# GitHub Issue #66

## Title
Add a thinking_level input (default: pi's medium)

## Description
Follow-up to #51 ([comparison](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/issues/51#issuecomment-6863264436)). pi picks a thinking level in this order: the model's scoped `thinkingLevel`, then the per-model setting, then `defaultThinkingLevel`, then `DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL = "medium"` (`pi-coding-agent/dist/core/defaults.js`, `model-resolver.js`). pi-action never sets one, so pi-durable's `resolveAgent` uses `state?.thinkingLevel ?? "off"`. Every run is **off**, even with `model_reasoning: true`. pi has no setting that matches this.

## Proposal

- **New input:** `thinking_level`, one of `off | minimal | low | medium | high | xhigh` (pi-ai's `ModelThinkingLevel`). Default `medium`.
- **Apply it on every run.** In `Thread.open`, add `thinkingLevel` to the `agent` that `configureAgent` passes to `root.configure`. A thread started under another level then switches on the next run, as the model does.
- **Models without reasoning.** When the model has no reasoning support (built-in model metadata, or `model_reasoning: false` for a custom model), send `off`, and write a log line instead of failing. pi does the same: it caps the level to what the model supports. Check how pi-ai maps levels for each provider (`thinkingLevelMap`, `compat_force_adaptive_thinking`, `supportsReasoningEffort`), and add a test with the faux provider that the level reaches the request options.
- **Release notes.** Mention it: the default moves runs from off to medium, so they may cost more tokens. This is a `feat` that matches pi. Set `thinking_level: off` to keep the old behavior.
- **Setup log.** Show the level in the `🤖` line (`🤖 anthropic/claude-… · thinking medium · …`).

## Tests and docs

- Tests:
  - Parsing the input, rejecting invalid values.
  - The configured `thinkingLevel` and the downgrade to `off` for models without reasoning.
  - A changed level on a continuing thread.
- Docs:
  - README inputs table, `docs/models.md` (a "Thinking" section), `action.yml`.

@pi please implement this and open a PR. Follow CONTRIBUTING.md, run `npm run check`, and update the docs.

## Important: Artifact and Script Requirements

**CRITICAL:** After the GitHub Action finishes running, all files modified or created are lost, and the GitHub Action runner is destroyed. Therefore:

1. **All generated code and artifacts MUST be committed** - Any files you create, modify, or generate must be committed and pushed to the repository before the action completes. Nothing will persist otherwise.

2. **Any throw-away scripts generated MUST be run immediately** - If you create temporary scripts (like `/tmp/create-issues.sh` or similar), you must execute them during the same session. They will be lost when the runner terminates.

3. **Commit and push all work** - Always end your work by committing and pushing changes to ensure they persist beyond the GitHub Action execution.
